title: Phase 3: Persist products in Motoko canister + fix storefront product fetch error + admin product list CRUD

requirements.text: Implement durable product persistence in the Motoko canister so that products created/updated/deleted via the admin panel are stored in stable canister memory and survive page reloads and canister upgrades.

quotes: Use Motoko canister memory to store products permanently
Products reload pe survive karein (no loss).

acceptanceCriteria: Products added via `adminAddProduct` remain available after browser refresh.
Products remain available after canister upgrade/redeploy (stable memory persistence).
Product updates via `adminUpdateProduct` are reflected in subsequent `publicListProducts`/`adminListProducts` results.
Product deletions via `adminDeleteProduct` remove the item from subsequent `publicListProducts`/`adminListProducts` results.
No changes violate the single-actor architecture (all logic remains in `backend/main.mo`; add upgrade hooks and/or `backend/migration.mo` only if required by state migration).

requirements.text: Ensure backend product APIs fully support the required product fields for Phase 3 persistence: name, price, description, image URLs, fabric, variants, blouse pairing, and category; and ensure `publicListProducts()` returns all persisted products for storefront usage.

quotes: On admin save: store product (name, price, desc, image URLs, fabric, variants, blouse pairing, category).
On page load (collections/category): fetch products from canister and display.

acceptanceCriteria: The backend product record includes fields for: `name`, `price`, `description`, `images`, `fabric`, `variants`, `blousePair`, `category`.
`publicListProducts()` returns the stored products without requiring admin auth.
`adminListProducts()` continues to require admin authorization and returns the same persisted products visible via `publicListProducts()`.

requirements.text: Fix the storefront "Could not fetch products from the backend" failure mode by correctly distinguishing between (a) empty catalog and (b) failed fetch; show an error toast only on real fetch failures, and show a premium empty state when the catalog is empty.

quotes: Fix "Could not fetch" error: If no products, show premium empty state: "No products yet — add in admin panel"
Error handling: show toast "Failed to load products. Try refreshing." if fetch fails.

acceptanceCriteria: When product fetch fails (e.g., canister/network error), show a toast with exact text: "Failed to load products. Try refreshing."
When the fetch succeeds but returns zero products, do not show the fetch-failed toast; instead show an empty state with the exact headline text: "No products yet — add in admin panel".
Storefront pages that depend on products (at minimum collections/category listing experiences that use `useGetAllProducts`) do not render blank screens or crash in either empty or error scenarios.
The old error presentation "Could not fetch products from the backend" is not shown to users in the normal UI flow.

requirements.text: Update `useGetAllProducts` (React Query) so it surfaces fetch failures to the UI (instead of silently returning an empty array), enabling pages to render a dedicated error state vs an empty-catalog state.

quotes: If no products, show premium empty state

acceptanceCriteria: On fetch failure, `useGetAllProducts` results in React Query error state (`isError`/`error`) rather than only returning an empty list.
On fetch failure, the toast with exact text "Failed to load products. Try refreshing." is shown once per failure event (no toast spam loops).
On success with zero products, `useGetAllProducts` is not in error state and returns an empty array.

requirements.text: Implement the premium empty-state UI for empty product catalog on collections/category pages: show "No products yet — add in admin panel" in gold text, and if the viewer is logged in as an admin, show a pearl-blue CTA button that navigates to the admin products page.

quotes: If no products, show premium empty state: "No products yet — add in admin panel" (gold text, pearl blue button to admin if logged in as admin).

acceptanceCriteria: Empty catalog state displays the exact text: "No products yet — add in admin panel".
The empty state matches the existing dark luxury theme, using gold-accent typography for the headline and premium card styling consistent with the app.
If and only if the user is recognized as an admin using the app’s existing admin detection approach (consistent with current admin gating logic), a visible pearl-blue button is rendered.
The admin CTA button navigates via SPA navigation to the admin products page route (existing admin route), without a full page reload.
If the user is not an admin, the admin CTA is not shown.

requirements.text: Ensure the admin panel product list shows all persisted products and supports edit/delete actions backed by canister persistence; deleting a product must remove it from canister storage and from the admin list after refresh.

quotes: Admin panel product list: Show all saved products with edit/delete buttons.

acceptanceCriteria: Admin products list loads products from the backend (`adminListProducts`) and reflects the canister’s persisted state.
Delete action calls the backend delete API and the product disappears from the list without requiring a manual reload.
After deleting a product, refreshing the page does not bring it back (it is removed from canister persistence).
Edit action updates the persisted product and the updated values are visible after refresh in both admin list and storefront listings (when applicable).

requirements.text: Apply/retain premium dark-luxury styling and golden hover/glow interactions for Phase 3 UI changes (empty state CTA, retry/error state actions, admin list actions), while keeping the app responsive and preventing blank screens/crashes.

quotes: Responsive, no blank screen or crash.

acceptanceCriteria: New/modified buttons added for Phase 3 have a gold hover/glow treatment consistent with existing styling utilities/classes.
All Phase 3-touched pages remain usable on mobile and desktop widths (no layout breakage or overflow causing horizontal scroll bugs).
No blank screen occurs when navigating to collections/category pages with empty catalog or when backend fetch fails.
No routing/authentication flow changes are introduced beyond linking to existing admin routes.

requirements.text: Add a Phase 3 verification step in the project documentation/release notes flow: after deployment, provide the draft/live URL and confirm a checklist proving persistence and error/empty states behave correctly.

quotes:
After update:
- Give draft/live URL.
- Confirm:
  - Products fetch from backend (no "Could not fetch" error).
  - Products save permanently (reload pe dikhte hain).
  - Admin list shows with edit/delete.
  - UI stable & impressive.

acceptanceCriteria: A post-deploy checklist is provided confirming: (1) products fetch from backend without the prior "Could not fetch" user-visible error, (2) persistence across reload, (3) admin list shows edit/delete, (4) UI remains stable/responsive.
The draft/live URL is provided after deployment.

constraints: Backend must remain a single-actor Motoko canister with all logic in `backend/main.mo`; add `backend/migration.mo` only if required for state upgrades.

Do not edit frontend files listed as immutable by the platform (e.g., `frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts(x)`, `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`, and `frontend/src/components/ui`).
Keep the existing dark luxury theme and existing routing/authentication flows; only add minimal UI necessary for Phase 3 (persistence + error/empty states + admin list correctness).
No external databases or third-party backends; persistence must be implemented using canister stable storage.
nonGoals: Adding new payment, shipping, or order-management features beyond what already exists.
Introducing real-time features (WebSockets/chat) or third-party auth providers beyond Internet Identity.
Adding new category taxonomy or redesigning non-product pages (dashboard/profile/login) beyond what is necessary to prevent regressions.
